survivors.locator: Article I — Of Faith in the Holy Trinity
survivors.phrase: in unity of this Godhead there are three persons, of one substance, power, and eternity
survivors.rationale: Affirms one Godhead (no division into separate gods) while distinguishing three persons (no collapse into one person), the classic non-confounding, non-dividing formula.
survivors.chunk_text: There is but one living and true God, everlasting, without body or parts, of infinite power, wisdom, and goodness; the maker and preserver of all things, both visible and invisible. And in unity of this Godhead there are three persons, of one substance, power, and eternity—the Father, the Son, and the Holy Ghost.

survivors.phrase: distinct but inseparable, eternally one in essence and power
survivors.rationale: Describes the Trinity's three persons as distinct (not confounded) yet inseparable and one in essence (not divided).
survivors.chunk_text: We believe in the one true, holy and living God, Eternal Spirit, who is Creator, Sovereign and Preserver of all things visible and invisible. He is infinite in power, wisdom, justice, goodness and love, and rules with gracious regard for the well-being and salvation of men, to the glory of his name. We believe the one God reveals himself as the Trinity: Father, Son and Holy Spirit, distinct but inseparable, eternally one in essence and power.

survivors.chunk_text: The Holy Ghost, proceeding from the Father and the Son, is of one substance, majesty, and glory with the Father and the Son, very and eternal God.

survivors.chunk_text: We believe in the Holy Spirit who proceeds from the Father and the Son, and is of the same essential nature, majesty, and glory, as the Father and the Son, truly and eternally God. He is ever present, assuring, preserving, guiding, and enabling the believer.
